122	class HTMLExtractor(htmlparser.HTMLParser):
123	    """
124	    Extract raw HTML from text.
125	
126	    The raw HTML is stored in the [`htmlStash`][markdown.util.HtmlStash] of the
127	    [`Markdown`][markdown.Markdown] instance passed to `md` and the remaining text
128	    is stored in `cleandoc` as a list of strings.
129	    """
130	
131	    def __init__(self, md: Markdown, *args, **kwargs):
132	        if 'convert_charrefs' not in kwargs:
133	            kwargs['convert_charrefs'] = False
134	
135	        # Block tags that should contain no content (self closing)
136	        self.empty_tags = set(['hr'])
137	
138	        self.lineno_start_cache = [0]
139	
140	        # This calls self.reset
141	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
142	        self.md = md
143	
144	    def reset(self):
145	        """Reset this instance.  Loses all unprocessed data."""
146	        self.inraw = False
147	        self.intail = False
148	        self.stack: list[str] = []  # When `inraw==True`, stack contains a list of tags
149	        self._cache: list[str] = []
150	        self.cleandoc: list[str] = []
151	        self.lineno_start_cache = [0]
152	
153	        super().reset()
154	
155	    def close(self):
156	        """Handle any buffered data."""
157	        super().close()
158	        if len(self.rawdata):
159	            # Temp fix for https://bugs.python.org/issue41989
160	            # TODO: remove this when the bug is fixed in all supported Python versions.
161	            if self.convert_charrefs and not self.cdata_elem:  # pragma: no cover
162	                self.handle_data(htmlparser.unescape(self.rawdata))
163	            else:
164	                self.handle_data(self.rawdata)
165	        # Handle any unclosed tags.
166	        if len(self._cache):
167	            self.cleandoc.append(self.md.htmlStash.store(''.join(self._cache)))
168	            self._cache = []
169	
170	    @property
171	    def line_offset(self) -> int:
172	        """Returns char index in `self.rawdata` for the start of the current line. """
173	        for ii in range(len(self.lineno_start_cache)-1, self.lineno-1):

176	            if lf_pos == -1:
177	                # No more newlines found. Use end of raw data as start of line beyond end.
178	                lf_pos = len(self.rawdata)
179	            self.lineno_start_cache.append(lf_pos+1)

183	    def at_line_start(self) -> bool:

188	        """

199

213	        if tag in self.empty_tags:
214	            self.handle_startendtag(tag, attrs)
215	            return
216	
217	        if self.md.is_block_level(tag) and (self.intail or (self.at_line_start() and not self.inraw)):

219	            self.inraw = True
220	            self.cleandoc.append('\n')
221	
222	        text = self.get_starttag_text()
223	        if self.inraw:
224	            self.stack.append(tag)
225	            self._cache.append(text)
226	        else:
227	            self.cleandoc.append(text)
228	            if tag in self.CDATA_CONTENT_ELEMENTS:
229	                # This is presumably a standalone tag in a code span (see #1036).
230	                self.clear_cdata_mode()

232	    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str):
233	        text = self.get_endtag_text(tag)
234	
235	        if self.inraw:
236	            self._cache.append(text)
237	            if tag in self.stack:
238	                # Remove tag from stack
239	                while self.stack:
240	                    if self.stack.pop() == tag:
241	                        break
242	            if len(self.stack) == 0:
243	                # End of raw block.
244	                if blank_line_re.match(self.rawdata[self.line_offset + self.offset + len(text):]):
245	                    # Preserve blank line and end of raw block.
246	                    self._cache.append('\n')
247	                else:
248	                    # More content exists after `endtag`.
249	                    self.intail = True
250	                # Reset stack.
251	                self.inraw = False
252	                self.cleandoc.append(self.md.htmlStash.store(''.join(self._cache)))
253	                # Insert blank line between this and next line.
254	                self.cleandoc.append('\n\n')
255	                self._cache = []
256	        else:
257	            self.cleandoc.append(text)
258	
259	    def handle_data(self, data: str):
260	        if self.intail and '\n' in data:
261	            self.intail = False
262	        if self.inraw:
263	            self._cache.append(data)
264	        else:
265	            self.cleandoc.append(data)
266	
267	    def handle_empty_tag(self, data: str, is_block: bool):
268	        """ Handle empty tags (`<data>`). """
269	        if self.inraw or self.intail:
270	            # Append this to the existing raw block
271	            self._cache.append(data)
272	        elif self.at_line_start() and is_block:
273	            # Handle this as a standalone raw block
274	            if blank_line_re.match(self.rawdata[self.line_offset + self.offset + len(data):]):
275	                # Preserve blank line after tag in raw block.
276	                data += '\n'
277	            else:
278	                # More content exists after tag.
279	                self.intail = True
280	            item = self.cleandoc[-1] if self.cleandoc else ''
281	            # If we only have one newline before block element, add another
282	            if not item.endswith('\n\n') and item.endswith('\n'):
283	                self.cleandoc.append('\n')
284	            self.cleandoc.append(self.md.htmlStash.store(data))
285	            # Insert blank line between this and next line.
286	            self.cleandoc.append('\n\n')
287	        else:
288	            self.cleandoc.append(data)
289	
290	    def handle_startendtag(self, tag: str, attrs):
291	        self.handle_empty_tag(self.get_starttag_text(), is_block=self.md.is_block_level(tag))
292	
293	    def handle_charref(self, name: str):
294	        self.handle_empty_tag('&#{};'.format(name), is_block=False)
295	
296	    def handle_entityref(self, name: str):
297	        self.handle_empty_tag('&{};'.format(name), is_block=False)
298	
299	    def handle_comment(self, data: str):
300	        # Check if the comment is unclosed, if so, we need to override position
301	        self.handle_empty_tag('<!--{}-->'.format(data), is_block=True)
302	
303	    def handle_decl(self, data: str):
304	        self.handle_empty_tag('<!{}>'.format(data), is_block=True)
305	
306	    def handle_pi(self, data: str):
307	        self.handle_empty_tag('<?{}?>'.format(data), is_block=True)
308	
309	    def unknown_decl(self, data: str):
310	        end = ']]>' if data.startswith('CDATA[') else ']>'
311	        self.handle_empty_tag('<![{}{}'.format(data, end), is_block=True)
312	
313	    def parse_pi(self, i: int) -> int:
314	        if self.at_line_start() or self.intail:
315	            return super().parse_pi(i)
316	        # This is not the beginning of a raw block so treat as plain data
317	        # and avoid consuming any tags which may follow (see #1066).
318	        self.handle_data('<?')
319	        return i + 2
320	
321	    # Internal -- parse comment, return length or -1 if not terminated
322	    # see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#comment-start-state
323	    def parse_comment(self, i, report=True):
324	        rawdata = self.rawdata
325	        assert rawdata.startswith('<!--', i), 'unexpected call to parse_comment()'
326	        match = commentclose.search(rawdata, i+4)
327	        if not match:
328	            self.handle_data('<')
329	            return i + 1
330	        if report:
331	            j = match.start()
332	            self.handle_comment(rawdata[i+4: j])
333	        return match.end()
334	
335	    def parse_html_declaration(self, i: int) -> int:
336	        if self.at_line_start() or self.intail:
337	            if self.rawdata[i:i+3] == '<![' and not self.rawdata[i:i+9] == '<![CDATA[':
338	                # We have encountered the bug in #1534 (Python bug `gh-77057`).
339	                # Provide an override until we drop support for Python < 3.13.
340	                result = self.parse_bogus_comment(i)
341	                if result == -1:
342	                    self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 1])
343	                    return i + 1
344	                return result
345	            return super().parse_html_declaration(i)
346	        # This is not the beginning of a raw block so treat as plain data
347	        # and avoid consuming any tags which may follow (see #1066).
348	        self.handle_data('<!')
349	        return i + 2
350	
351	    def parse_bogus_comment(self, i: int, report: int = 0) -> int:
352	        # Override the default behavior so that bogus comments get passed
353	        # through unaltered by setting `report` to `0` (see #1425).
354	        pos = super().parse_bogus_comment(i, report)
355	        if pos == -1:  # pragma: no cover
356	            return -1
357	        self.handle_empty_tag(self.rawdata[i:pos], is_block=False)
358	        return pos
359	
360	    # The rest has been copied from base class in standard lib to address #1036.
361	    # As `__startag_text` is private, all references to it must be in this subclass.
362	    # The last few lines of `parse_starttag` are reversed so that `handle_starttag`
363	    # can override `cdata_mode` in certain situations (in a code span).
364	    __starttag_text: str | None = None
365	
366	    def get_starttag_text(self) -> str:
367	        """Return full source of start tag: `<...>`."""
368	        return self.__starttag_text
369	
370	    def parse_starttag(self, i: int) -> int:  # pragma: no cover
371	        # Treat `</>` as normal data as it is not a real tag.
372	        if self.rawdata[i:i + 3] == '</>':
373	            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 3])
374	            return i + 3
375	
376	        self.__starttag_text = None
377	        endpos = self.check_for_whole_start_tag(i)
378	        if endpos < 0:
379	            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 1])
380	            return i + 1
381	        rawdata = self.rawdata
382	        self.__starttag_text = rawdata[i:endpos]
383	
384	        # Now parse the data between `i+1` and `j` into a tag and `attrs`
385	        attrs = []
386	        match = htmlparser.tagfind_tolerant.match(rawdata, i+1)
387	        assert match, 'unexpected call to parse_starttag()'
388	        k = match.end()
389	        self.lasttag = tag = match.group(1).lower()
390	        while k < endpos:
391	            m = htmlparser.attrfind_tolerant.match(rawdata, k)
392	            if not m:
393	                break
394	            attrname, rest, attrvalue = m.group(1, 2, 3)
395	            if not rest:
396	                attrvalue = None
397	            elif attrvalue[:1] == '\'' == attrvalue[-1:] or \
398	                 attrvalue[:1] == '"' == attrvalue[-1:]:  # noqa: E127
399	                attrvalue = attrvalue[1:-1]
400	            if attrvalue:
401	                attrvalue = htmlparser.unescape(attrvalue)
402	            attrs.append((attrname.lower(), attrvalue))
403	            k = m.end()
404	
405	        end = rawdata[k:endpos].strip()
406	        if end not in (">", "/>"):
407	            lineno, offset = self.getpos()
408	            if "\n" in self.__starttag_text:
409	                lineno = lineno + self.__starttag_text.count("\n")
410	                offset = len(self.__starttag_text) \
411	                         - self.__starttag_text.rfind("\n")  # noqa: E127
412	            else:
413	                offset = offset + len(self.__starttag_text)
414	            self.handle_data(rawdata[i:endpos])
415	            return endpos
416	        if end.endswith('/>'):
417	            # XHTML-style empty tag: `<span attr="value" />`
418	            self.handle_startendtag(tag, attrs)
419	        else:
420	            # *** set `cdata_mode` first so we can override it in `handle_starttag` (see #1036) ***
421	            if tag in self.CDATA_CONTENT_ELEMENTS:
422	                self.set_cdata_mode(tag)
423	            self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)
424	        return endpos

A copy is imported rather than the module being directly imported as this ensures that the user can import
and  use the unmodified library for their own needs.

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import importlib.util
import sys
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Sequence

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
    from markdown import Markdown

# Included for versions which do not have current comment fix
commentclose = re.compile(r'--!?>')

# Import a copy of the html.parser lib as `htmlparser` so we can monkeypatch it.
# Users can still do `from html import parser` and get the default behavior.
spec = importlib.util.find_spec('html.parser')
htmlparser = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(htmlparser)
sys.modules['htmlparser'] = htmlparser

# This is a hack. We are sneaking in `</>` so we can capture it without the HTML parser
# throwing it away. When we see it, we will process it as data.
htmlparser.starttagopen = re.compile('<[a-zA-Z]|</>')

htmlparser.endtagopen = re.compile('</[a-zA-Z]?')

# Monkeypatch `HTMLParser` to only accept `?>` to close Processing Instructions.
htmlparser.piclose = re.compile(r'\?>')
# Monkeypatch `HTMLParser` to only recognize entity references with a closing semicolon.
htmlparser.entityref = re.compile(r'&([a-zA-Z][-.a-zA-Z0-9]*);')
# Monkeypatch `HTMLParser` to no longer support partial entities. We are always feeding a complete block,
# so the 'incomplete' functionality is unnecessary. As the `entityref` regex is run right before incomplete,
# and the two regex are the same, then incomplete will simply never match and we avoid the logic within.
htmlparser.incomplete = htmlparser.entityref
# Monkeypatch `HTMLParser` to not accept a backtick in a tag name, attribute name, or bare value.
htmlparser.locatestarttagend_tolerant = re.compile(r"""
  <[a-zA-Z][^`\t\n\r\f />\x00]*       # tag name <= added backtick here
  (?:[\s/]*                           # optional whitespace before attribute name
    (?:(?<=['"\s/])[^`\s/>][^\s/=>]*  # attribute name <= added backtick here
      (?:\s*=+\s*                     # value indicator
        (?:'[^']*'                    # LITA-enclosed value
          |"[^"]*"                    # LIT-enclosed value
          |(?!['"])[^`>\s]*           # bare value <= added backtick here
         )
         (?:\s*,)*                    # possibly followed by a comma
       )?(?:\s|/(?!>))*
     )*
   )?
  \s*                                 # trailing whitespace
""", re.VERBOSE)
htmlparser.locatetagend = re.compile(r"""
  [a-zA-Z][^`\t\n\r\f />]*           # tag name
  [\t\n\r\f /]*                     # optional whitespace before attribute name
  (?:(?<=['"\t\n\r\f /])[^`\t\n\r\f />][^\t\n\r\f /=>]*  # attribute name
    (?:=                            # value indicator
      (?:'[^']*'                    # LITA-enclosed value
        |"[^"]*"                    # LIT-enclosed value
        |(?!['"])[^>\t\n\r\f ]*     # bare value
       )
     )?
    [\t\n\r\f /]*                   # possibly followed by a space
   )*
   >?
""", re.VERBOSE)

# Match a blank line at the start of a block of text (two newlines).
# The newlines may be preceded by additional whitespace.
blank_line_re = re.compile(r'^([ ]*\n){2}')


class _HTMLParser(htmlparser.HTMLParser):
    """Handle special start and end tags."""

    def parse_endtag(self, i):
        start = self.rawdata[i:i+3]
        c = ord(start[-1])
        is_data = len(start) < 3 or not (65 <= c <= 90 or 97 <= c <= 122)
        pos = super().parse_endtag(i) if not is_data else -1
        if pos == -1:
            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 2])
            return i + 2
        return pos

    def parse_starttag(self, i: int) -> int:  # pragma: no cover
        # Treat `</>` as normal data as it is not a real tag.
        if self.rawdata[i:i + 3] == '</>':
            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 3])
            return i + 3

        return super().parse_starttag(i)


# Overwrite our custom one for people like MkDocs that pull it in
htmlparser.HTMLParser = _HTMLParser


class HTMLExtractor(htmlparser.HTMLParser):

The bug is fixed: the `<picture>` example from the report now renders as a single paragraph with the comment left in place.

**Cause:** in `markdown/htmlparser.py`, `handle_empty_tag` treated any comment at the start of a line as a standalone raw HTML block. It did this even when the comment sat inside an open inline element such as `<picture>`, and so forced a paragraph break after it.

**Fix:** the parser now tracks inline tags opened in the current paragraph. A comment at line start is kept inline when one of those tags is still open and its closing tag appears later in the same paragraph. The same applies to processing instructions, declarations and CDATA, which went through the same code path.

Comments that are not inside such an element behave as before, including `foo\n<!-- c -->\nbar` and a comment following a stray `<span>` in a code span.

**Tests:** I added three regression tests to `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py`; that file passes (127 tests).

The full suite cannot run cleanly in this venv as-is: `tests/test_apis.py` needs `yaml`, and the built-in extensions are not registered by short name, so 166 extension tests fail on import regardless of this change. With a temporary shim resolving those names, everything else passed (705 passed, 110 skipped, plus all 201 `md_in_html` tests); that run was before I added the three new tests. The shim is removed, and `test_apis.py` was not run.
